##### Project general facts

Munduk Horizont is a boutique wellness resort of private villas designed by Edward Bryan Architecture and run as a single short-term rental resort by the developer's own team. The villas step down a forested slope in a staggered layout, and the buildings cover only a small part of the site, leaving most of the land as garden linked by paths and steps. The resort consists of identical one-bedroom wellness villas, each with a living room, a bedroom under a double-height ceiling, a bathroom and a view terrace. Investment is offered as shares in the company that owns and operates the hotel complex rather than as the purchase of individual villas, and the land is held on a long-term leasehold.

Wellness is built into every villa: a private Finnish sauna and a hot tub on the terrace give guests their own spa routine with the valley in view. A shared spa zone adds massage and treatment rooms, set in a glass-walled spa pavilion and a treatment room that looks out over the valley. Social life gathers around a pavilion with a fire pit and grill, where fireside dinners are hosted, while a reception with a kitchen greets guests at the entrance. Resort services include housekeeping and grounds care, airport transfers and organised excursions to the surrounding lakes and waterfalls, and a shared car park sits beside the access road. From the terraces, the villas look out over the valley towards the sea.

Interiors are finished in ulin, a dense Indonesian ironwood, giving the villas a warm natural timber character. Panoramic glazing running from floor to roof faces north-west and opens the living room and bedroom to the view, while adjustable heating keeps the rooms comfortable in the cool mountain air. The living area combines lounge seating with a dining table and a fitted kitchen, and an internal staircase and wardrobe complete the layout. Villas are delivered turnkey, fully furnished and equipped with furniture, appliances, linens and lighting, together with the sauna, hot tub and landscaping, so they are ready to receive guests without further fit-out.

##### Location description and benefits

Munduk is a highland village in the mountains of North Bali, surrounded by forested ridges, waterfalls and plantations of coffee, clove and vanilla. Its altitude gives the area a cool, fresh climate that sets it apart from the warm coastal resorts of the south. The Bedugul area lies a short drive away, with Lake Beratan and the Ulun Danu temple on its shore, the Handara golf club and padel courts, while the lakes of Buyan and Tamblingan stretch through the hills close to the village.

The surroundings are known for waterfalls such as Melanting, Banyumala and Sekumpul, and for the agricultural landscape of the highlands. The Jatiluwih rice terraces, a UNESCO World Heritage site, are within driving distance, and Bali Farm House offers a family outing with its alpaca farm. The mountain road through Bedugul and Mengwi connects Munduk with Canggu and the southern part of the island, and Ngurah Rai International Airport is reached by the same route. Daily life follows a quiet village rhythm, with nature, lake trips and plantation visits at its centre.

Cool air, lakes, waterfalls and a slower pace give the North Bali highlands a distinct appeal for travellers looking for nature and wellness stays away from the busy beach towns. This makes the area relevant for buyers interested in boutique short-term rental accommodation in a mountain setting rather than on the crowded coast. As elsewhere in Bali, foreign buyers acquire property on leasehold terms, so the highlands offer an alternative location within the same ownership framework as the established southern resort areas.
